back: The death benefit stated in the life insurance policy.
Paid to the beneficiary upon the insured's death.
The premium is based on the face amount: $$\text{Annual Premium} = \frac{\text{Face Amount}}{1{,}000} \times \text{Rate per } \$1{,}000$$
The periodic payment made by the insured to keep the policy in force.
Can be paid annually, semiannually, quarterly, or monthly.
[[imp:More frequent payments usually cost more per year due to administrative fees.]]
Temporary coverage for a specified period (1, 5, 10, 20 years).
Cheapest form; no cash value.
If the insured outlives the term, the policy expires with no value.

cards.front: Calculate term insurance premium for $200,000 face, age 40, rate $3.52 per $1,000.
back: Payable each year of the term.
Permanent protection for the insured's entire life.
Premiums are higher than term because a portion funds a [[kw:cash value]] savings component.
The premium remains level for life.

cards.front: Compute the annual premium for $150,000 straight life at rate $12 per $1,000.

back: Permanent coverage with premiums paid for only 20 years.
After 20 years, the policy is [[kw:paid‑up]] – no more premiums are due.
Cash value builds faster than straight life.
Premiums stop after 20 years, often before retirement.
Total outlay can be less than paying straight life for many decades.
Provides lifetime coverage with a limited payment period.
The savings element of permanent life insurance that accumulates over time.
It can be borrowed against or used for nonforfeiture options.
[[imp:Cash value is not added to the face amount at death; the beneficiary receives only the face amount.]]
1. Cash surrender – receive accumulated cash value; policy ends.
2. Reduced paid‑up insurance – use cash value to buy a smaller permanent policy with no further premiums.
3. Extended term insurance – use cash value to buy term insurance for the full face amount for a limited time.

cards.front: Cash value is $8,000. The rate for paid‑up insurance is $200 per $1,000. How much reduced paid‑up insurance can be purchased?
back: She would have $40,000 of paid‑up permanent insurance.

cards.front: True or False: Term insurance builds cash value.
back: False. Term insurance is pure protection with no savings component.
Only permanent insurance (straight life, 20‑payment life, etc.) builds cash value.
